Updated request scope as of 5/17/24 refinement sent by Mr.Small:

We have put some thought into search restrictions and terms and here is what we would suggest:

(1) total time range of January 1, 2023 through July 31, 2023
(2) Anything that includes Juli Beth Hinds, Dr. Amy Lerner, urban studies and planning (USP), global policy & strategy (GPS), UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms
(3) Anything related to the regional water equity report or RDF
(4) Anything containing a reference to "Juli Beth Hinds, Dr Amy Lerner,  Geosyntec, USP, GPS, or the RWER or RDF", UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms sent to or from "Elise Ruiz, anyone at Murakawa Communications, anyone at Geosyntec including but not limited to Ken Susillo, Megan Otto, Stephanie Zinn; and anyone at the County including but not limited to Stephanie Gaines, Crystal Benham, Todd Snyder, Sarah Agassi, Eden Brukman, and Murtaza Baxamusa"

Original Request:

To Whom it may Concern:
I am writing on behalf of my client Juli Beth Hinds. On behalf of Ms. Hinds, please consider this a formal request pursuant to California Public Records Act, Government Code §6250 et seq. for copies of all DOCUMENTS of the County of San Diego Land Use & Environment Group that reference or relate to: Juli Beth Hinds; the Department of Urban Studies and Planning at the University of California San Diego; or Nathan Fletcher. ("DOCUMENTS" as used herein, shall be defined to mean any ''writing'' as that term is defined in Evidence Code section 250, including, but not limited to, correspondence, emails, texts, communications of any kind, recordings, tapes, computer print-outs, records, slides, photographs, notes, working papers, written analyses, memoranda, plans, telegraphs, telexes and transcriptions, electronic data, and notes or memoranda made by any telephone communications.) This request encompasses all DOCUMENTS dated or created between the dates of January 1, 2022 through the date of this letter.
I request delivery of these records to our firm's office, located at 402 W. Broadway, Suite 1270, San Diego, CA 92101, or we can arrange to pick them up at a reasonable location designated by the County.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

From:                                                       Leroy, Chiara

Subject:                                                   List of Equity Impact Grant Winners - Cohort #1

Good morning Barbara,

It was so nice spending time with you on Wednesday, catching up and talking shop. As promised, here
is the list of Equity Impact Grant winners for cohort #1. The cohort #2 winners should be announced
next week or so.
Building Justice (HoMEwork) – A Southeast San Diego organization that supports people
transitioning out of incarceration by prioritizing their personal development, creating a support
system, and providing opportunities to amplify their voices and inﬂuence policy decisions.
First Gen Scholars – An organization helping ﬁrst-generation, low-income Black, Latinx, and
Southeast Asian students navigate the college admissions process and graduate debt-free.
Free Thought Revolution – A community-driven eﬀort to “bridge the divide of humanity
through storytelling, community, and social action.” In addition to their podcast, their vision
includes educational initiatives and housing programs to provide a safe space for marginalized
individuals to engage in healing and community-building.
Garden 31 – This organization trains and mentors youth and adults that are considered at-risk,
formerly incarcerated, justice-impacted, and socioeconomically disadvantaged in regenerative
agriculture, sustainable food systems, and life skills to improve community health and wellness.
Inner-Tribal Treatment – To address the needs of the Native American population impacted by
the opioid crisis, this organization provides one of the only culturally-based treatment
programs in Southern California.
Lived Experiences – A North County community-based organization that utilizes data-proven
methods to advocate for change by investing in people’s microsystems and addressing the root
causes of physical and emotional trauma.
Majdal Arab Community Center of San Diego – Through advocacy and cultural programs, this
East County organization works to empower and uplift the Arab community in San Diego.
Paddle for Peace – An organization conceived to create a nurturing space where BIPOC children
could not only access coastal environments for recreation, physical ﬁtness and mental healing
but also envision and explore careers in Marine Biology and Environmentalism. To date, they
have provided over 600 ﬁrst time coastal experiences for BIPOC, underserved youth.
San Diego Community Birth Center – This is the only Black-owned birth center in San Diego
County, providing access to midwifery care, doula and lactation services, among other
resources that ensure healthy births.
San Diego Black LGBTQ Coalition – A volunteer-led organization that not only serves over 500
Black LGBTQ people and families yearly but works to address the acute needs of the Black
transgender community.

Sharing some additional resources that may be of use:
Community Leadership Teams, including links to each region’s website (which has each region’s
priority areas listed), and the 2008-2025 Community Health Assessments
Equity Impact Report, provides “baseline synopsis of the impact of systemic racial inequities
throughout our County”

Please let me know if there’s anything else that I can share with you.
Talk soon and good luck canvassing!

Warmly,

Chiara

Dear Murtaza, Rebeca and Nicole,

Thanks for the very useful conversation today.  As follow-up, I’ve drafted the attached concept note on what benchmarking the County’s efforts against the SDGs could look like.  I stress that this is meant to be complementary to the existing sustainability framework used by the county, but the benefit is that it benchmarks the county’s progress against internationally-recognized goals for environmental sustainability and social inclusion.

I’d be eager to hear your feedback and incorporate your advice.  I’m excited about a data-driven, integrated strategic planning process to meet the SDGs, using the common framework they provide and the quantitative 2030 as an useful organizing principle for some of our conversations (again, as a complement to existing county vision and goals around sustainability).  The SDGs also open the door to strategic collaborations with other jurisdictions in the region to meet the SDGs (including the City of San Diego, which has announced it wants to do a VLR but has not yet started).

Regards,

Gordon

Hi Elise,

Thank you for this!

For the first topic in the deep dives flyer, can you add “Financial Risks & Investments for water sustainability” or something of that nature? At first glance, people may think it’s a general financial literacy class, unless that is what it’s going to be?

Also, are you available to connect tomorrow afternoon or early next week to talk about our TCC Planning Grant application?

Thank you!

Carmina

Subject: RE: Connect with OSEJ Team & Next Steps

Hello all,

Thank you for your time and for the thoughtful discussion yesterday! Our team really appreciated the opportunity to connect with you all.

As I mentioned during the meeting, I am happy to meet and discuss the Regional Water Equity effort in more detail. I have attached the Project Fact Sheet and the flyer for the virtual Deep Dive events to share with your communities, and we have these documents translated in the threshold languages, which I can send to you separately.

The Deep Dive series is scheduled through the beginning of September, and we appreciate you sharing the flyer with your networks to inform communities about these events, as their feedback is greatly valued on this topic. You can also refer to the Regional Water Equity website <https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/osej/waterequity/>  to stay informed on upcoming events and project updates. We will continue to stay connected with you and please feel free to let us know if you have any questions.

Have a great evening!

Elise
